what: Ecolab sells cleaning, sanitising and water treatment programmes. It supplies the chemicals, the dispensing equipment and the service staff that keep restaurants, hotels, hospitals and factories clean and their water systems running.
customers: Restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food processors, breweries, data centres and heavy industry in most countries.
money: water treatment, paper and food processing chemicals
cleaning and sanitising for restaurants, hotels and healthcare
moat: Service technicians who visit customer sites regularly, equipment installed on the customer's premises, and programmes written into food safety audits.
risks: Growth has been slow at about 2% in the last financial year
Raw material and energy costs feed directly into margins
Restaurant and hotel demand follows consumer spending
Water treatment competes with large industrial gas and chemical groups
opportunities: Data centre cooling needs large volumes of treated water, a new and growing market for it
Pricing has outpaced raw material costs, lifting gross margins
Customers under water scarcity rules need its efficiency programmes
watch: Organic sales growth and gross margin, which show whether pricing is still ahead of costs.
